clockModel.explanation: The two guests do not have precision-synchronised clocks. The walkthrough is a causal replay built from per-process event order, validated packet direction, work-request relationships, completion relationships and explicit control-channel messages—not a nanosecond-accurate distributed trace.

walkthrough.explanation: The application opens a verbs context. Pyverbs is a Python binding to the same RDMA verbs interface used by native RDMA applications.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Python asks verbs for a handle to the rxe0 device.
teachingPoints: A verbs context is the application's handle to an RDMA device.
Soft-RoCE implements the transport in software for learning; the verbs model is real.
walkthrough.title: Open the Soft-RoCE device

codeRefs.label: Query port and select RoCEv2 GID

walkthrough.explanation: RoCEv2 uses IP-address-derived GIDs. These GIDs are later programmed into the queue pair so the transport knows how to reach the peer.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Each host discovers the RoCEv2 GID for its data interface.
walkthrough.title: Find the RoCEv2 GID

walkthrough.explanation: The memory registration produces local and remote keys. The QP starts in RESET. The CQ is where the application later observes completions; it is not a network packet.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Before data can move, each endpoint creates a protection domain, registers memory, creates a completion queue, and creates a reliable-connected queue pair.
teachingPoints: LKEY authorises local access by the RNIC; RKEY is shared for authorised remote access.
A QP has a send queue and a receive queue.
walkthrough.title: Create PD, MR, CQ and QP

walkthrough.explanation: This control-channel exchange does not carry application payload. It merely gives each endpoint the values needed to program its QP. The RDMA data captures contain only the separate data interface.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The hosts exchange QPN, initial PSN and GID over a small TCP control channel.
walkthrough.title: Exchange endpoint metadata

walkthrough.explanation: INIT enables the port and access flags. RTR installs the peer QPN, peer initial send PSN and route. RTS installs the local initial send PSN and retry behaviour. Only RTS permits data work requests.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Each QP is programmed first with local properties, then peer receive properties, then send properties.
walkthrough.title: Drive the QP RESET → INIT → RTR → RTS

walkthrough.explanation: Because no SEND, WRITE or READ work request is posted, there is no corresponding RDMA data-transfer pcap for Experiment A. FabricLab does not invent one.

teachingPoints: The absence of a capture is evidence of correct scope, not missing functionality.

experiments.title: Two-Sided RDMA: SEND and RECEIVE

codeRefs.label: Create resources and connect control channel

walkthrough.explanation: The receiver's buffer is where inbound SEND payload bytes can land. The sender has its own source buffer. These are different memory regions on different hosts.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Both endpoints register memory and create a reliable-connected QP.
walkthrough.title: Create matching endpoint resources

walkthrough.explanation: Each side programs its QP using the peer's local QPN and initial send PSN. The endpoint QPNs in this recording are genuinely asymmetric.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: TCP carries connection metadata, never the RDMA payload.
walkthrough.title: Exchange QPN, PSN and GID

codeRefs.label: Post receive WR and signal readiness

walkthrough.explanation: A receive WR is required for two-sided SEND/RECEIVE. It contains buffer location and length; it does not contain payload. Posting it does not put a packet on the wire.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The receiver tells its QP where a future inbound SEND may land.
teachingPoints: The WR ID is application/verbs metadata. It is not a BTH packet field.
LKEY is local memory access metadata. It is not carried as the remote RKEY in RDMA packets.
walkthrough.title: Receiver posts a receive work request

walkthrough.explanation: The send WR describes the local buffer using an LKEY and requests a signalled completion. Only now does the transport have work that can become a network packet.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: After the peer says its receive queue is armed, Host A copies the payload into registered memory and posts a SEND WR.
walkthrough.title: Sender posts a signalled SEND

walkthrough.explanation: The captured BTH destination QPN is the receiver's local QPN. The PSN comes from the sender QP's send sequence. Select the packet to inspect the exact decoded fields from this run.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Soft-RoCE emits a genuine RoCEv2 SEND Only packet to UDP port 4791.
walkthrough.title: SEND Only packet crosses the data network

codeRefs.label: Poll receive completion and verify payload

walkthrough.explanation: The receive CQE is a local completion-queue record, not a network packet. The application validates that the bytes in memory exactly match the expected payload.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host B receives the bytes in the buffer described by its receive WR and observes a receive completion.
walkthrough.title: Receiver memory and receive completion

walkthrough.explanation: This replay does not claim nanosecond ordering of the two hosts' application completion processing. The protocol dependency is narrower: the SEND request must reach the responder before the responder can acknowledge it, and the sender completion is observed on Host A's own CQ.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The responder transport returns an ACK addressed to the sender's local QPN, and Host A observes its signalled send completion.
walkthrough.title: ACK returns; sender completion is local

experiments.title: One-Sided RDMA: Writing Directly Into Remote Memory

codeRefs.label: Initialise target buffer and register memory

walkthrough.explanation: Registration pins the memory in the verbs domain and produces keys. The initial bytes are evidence for the before state; no network packet has been sent.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host B fills a buffer with a known pattern and registers it with remote-write permission.
walkthrough.title: Target prepares remote-writable memory

walkthrough.explanation: This metadata authorises and locates remote access. The control message does not contain the WRITE payload and does not mutate memory.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The target shares its memory address, length and RKEY over the TCP control channel.
teachingPoints: RKEY is shared remote-access metadata. LKEY remains local to each endpoint.
The two endpoint QPNs are independent and asymmetric in this recording.
walkthrough.title: Target shares address and RKEY

walkthrough.explanation: The forward WRITE packet will name the target's local QPN. The reverse ACK will name the writer's local QPN. Confusing those directions is a common RDMA diagnostic mistake.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The writer QP knows the target QPN and initial packet sequence state.
walkthrough.title: Both queue pairs reach RTS

walkthrough.explanation: The work request combines local source metadata (address and LKEY) with remote destination metadata (address and RKEY). The WR ID is not a packet header field.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host A posts a signalled WR whose local SGE points to its source buffer and whose remote fields name Host B memory.
walkthrough.title: Writer posts one RDMA WRITE work request

walkthrough.explanation: Select the packet inspector to compare the RETH address and RKEY with the metadata Host B shared. They match because both came from the same validated run; they are not hard-coded teaching constants.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The genuine capture contains one RDMA WRITE Only packet carrying the target VA, RKEY, DMA length and payload bytes.
walkthrough.title: RDMA WRITE Only packet crosses UDP/4791

walkthrough.explanation: Host B posted no receive work request. Ordinary RDMA WRITE does not consume a target receive WR and does not generate a normal receive CQE on the target. The mutation is performed by the RDMA transport, not by the TCP control channel.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The Soft-RoCE transport writes the payload directly into Host B's registered memory.
teachingPoints: This is the defining one-sided property of RDMA WRITE.
WRITE with immediate data has different receive-side semantics and is not what this experiment uses.
walkthrough.title: Remote memory changes without a receive WR

codeRefs.label: Poll writer completion and signal target

walkthrough.explanation: The completion means the initiator's requested WRITE operation completed successfully. It is not evidence that the remote application has consumed the data, and it is not a target receive CQE.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The target transport acknowledges the request, and Host A receives its own signalled completion.
walkthrough.title: ACK returns and writer completion is local

codeRefs.label: Synchronise, poll target CQ, verify memory

walkthrough.explanation: The target polls its CQ and observes zero completions, then verifies the payload. The control message is a notification mechanism only; it neither carried the payload nor caused the memory mutation.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Only after an explicit application-level control message does Host B inspect memory.
walkthrough.title: Separate synchronisation lets the target verify memory

experiments.title: One-Sided RDMA: Reading Remote Memory

codeRefs.label: Populate source memory and create resources

walkthrough.explanation: The source application makes memory readable remotely by sharing the address and RKEY. No responder application work request will be posted for the later transport response.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host B writes a known secret into its buffer, registers the memory, and records the before snapshot.
walkthrough.title: Source populates registered memory

codeRefs.label: Share metadata and bring QP to RTS

walkthrough.explanation: This control exchange authorises the later read. It does not transfer the secret payload.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Address, length and RKEY travel over TCP as connection metadata.
walkthrough.title: Source shares read-access metadata

walkthrough.explanation: The local SGE uses the reader's LKEY; the remote address and RKEY describe the source memory. READ is still initiated from the send queue even though data ultimately flows back toward the reader.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host A posts a WR describing its own destination buffer and the remote source range.
walkthrough.title: Reader posts an RDMA READ work request

walkthrough.explanation: The packet names the responder's local QPN. At this point no payload bytes have returned to Host A.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: A genuine READ Request packet carries the remote VA, RKEY and DMA length toward Host B.
walkthrough.title: READ Request packet asks the source transport for data

walkthrough.explanation: The responder application did not post a send WR for this response. The response is generated by the RDMA transport because READ is a request/response operation. Its destination QPN is the reader's local QPN and its PSN begins at the originating request PSN.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host B's RDMA transport reads the authorised memory and returns the data in a response packet.
walkthrough.title: Responder transport returns READ Response Only

codeRefs.label: Poll read completion and verify bytes

walkthrough.explanation: The completion is local to the reader. It is correlated to the application WR by WR ID and to the response by protocol causality, not by pretending that the two VM clocks are precisely synchronised.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: Host A observes a successful RDMA read completion and verifies the bytes that landed in its local buffer.
walkthrough.title: Reader completion and payload verification

codeRefs.label: Source waits and confirms no CQE

walkthrough.explanation: The responder side of an RDMA READ does not post a WR, so there is no responder application CQE. This is transport behaviour, not a missing event in the evidence.
walkthrough.simpleExplanation: The source receives a later control-channel notification and confirms that its application CQ remained empty.
walkthrough.title: Source application observes no completion
